commitResults.messageTitle: Duke.java: Greet user and exit with BOT identity
commitResults.messageBody:
Implements the Level-0 requirement: print a banner, greet the user
by name, and print a goodbye message on exit. Renamed the chatbot
from Duke to BOT and updated the ASCII banner to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: Duke.java: Echo user commands until bye
commitResults.messageBody:
Implements the Level-1 requirement: read input in a loop and echo
each line back inside a divider block, exiting on the bye command.
Also switches to the indented divider/text format (4-space divider,
5-space text) for consistency across greet, echo, and exit output.

commitResults.messageTitle: Duke.java: Store and list user-entered tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Implements the Level-2 requirement: any input other than "list" or
"bye" is stored in a fixed-size array (capacity 100) and acknowledged
with "added: <text>"; "list" displays all stored items numbered.
No persistence to disk is needed at this stage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add mark/unmark commands and extract Task class
commitResults.messageBody:
Implements the Level-3 requirement: tasks can be marked done/not done
via "mark N" / "unmark N", and "list" now shows each task's status
icon. Extracted task state into a separate Task class (description,
isDone, getStatusIcon/markAsDone/markAsNotDone) per the A-Classes
extension, replacing the raw String[] storage in Duke.java.

Also ignore *.class files in .gitignore in case javac is run without
-d (compiling straight into src/main/java).

commitResults.messageTitle: Add test-ui skill and UI test plan; wire into AGENTS.md
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds a project skill (.claude/skills/test-ui) that builds Duke, runs
the console test cases recorded in test/ui-test-plan.md against it,
prints a transcript of each session, and stops immediately on the
first mismatch, reporting expected vs. actual output.

test/ui-test-plan.md currently covers: greet-and-exit, listing with
no tasks, adding a todo/deadline/event and listing them, and
mark/unmark. Manually walked through the skill's procedure end to end
and all 4 test cases pass against the current implementation.

AGENTS.md now instructs that after any src/main/java change, the test
plan should be updated if behavior changed, and the test-ui skill
should be invoked before considering the change complete.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Todo, Deadline, and Event task subclasses
commitResults.messageBody:
Each extends Task and overrides toString() to prepend its type icon
([T]/[D]/[E]) via super.toString(), per the A-Inheritance extension:
task-specific state (Deadline's "by", Event's "from"/"to") lives only
on the subclass, while shared description/done-status stays in Task.

commitResults.messageTitle: Duke.java: Support todo, deadline, and event commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds parsing for "todo <desc>", "deadline <desc> /by <when>", and
"event <desc> /from <start> /to <end>", storing them polymorphically
in the existing Task[] array. Each addition prints a confirmation
with the task's string form and the running task count. Replaces the
old catch-all free-text add from Level-2/3, which the Level-4 command
set no longer uses.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add error handling with a custom BotException
commitResults.messageBody:
Implements the Level-5 requirement (A-Exceptions extension): command
dispatch now validates input and throws BotException with a specific,
actionable message for an unrecognized command, a todo/deadline/event
missing its description or /by //from //to arguments, and a mark/unmark
with a missing, non-numeric, or out-of-range task number. Errors are
caught in main and printed inside the usual divider block instead of
crashing or silently doing nothing.

Adds Test Case 5 to test/ui-test-plan.md covering these error paths;
ran the test-ui skill and all 5 test cases pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add delete command and switch to ArrayList<Task>
commitResults.messageBody:
Implements the Level-6 requirement: "delete N" removes the Nth task
and reports its final state plus the new running task count, reusing
the existing parseTaskIndex validation shared with mark/unmark. Per
the A-Collections extension, task storage moves from a fixed-size
Task[100] to an ArrayList<Task>, removing the 100-task cap.

Updates test/ui-test-plan.md: adds Test Case 6 for the delete
happy path, extends Test Case 5 with delete's error paths, and adds
a trailing "list" to Test Case 5 so its "no task is added as a
result" claim is actually checked against output rather than assumed.
Ran the test-ui skill; all 6 test cases pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename chatbot class from Duke/BOT to Bot
commitResults.messageBody:
Duke.java was renamed to Bot.java earlier but never actually renamed;
this fixes that and also settles on "Bot" (proper-name casing) over
the all-caps "BOT" used in between, since it reads as a name rather
than an acronym. Updates every reference: the class/printed name,
test/ui-test-plan.md, the test-ui skill, and both README files.

Rebuilt and reran all 6 test-ui-plan test cases; all pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save tasks to ./data/bot.txt after every change (write path)
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds Task#toSaveFormat(), implemented by Todo/Deadline/Event, and a new
Storage class that serializes the task list to a pipe-separated line
per task (e.g. "T | 1 | read book"). Bot now calls Storage.save()
after every mutating command (todo, deadline, event, mark, unmark,
delete), creating ./data if needed. This is the write half of Level 7
save/load; loading the file back in on startup comes next.

Storage uses java.nio.file.Paths so the path is relative to the
project root and built with the correct separator on any OS, per the
Level 7 requirements. Also gitignore the generated ./data directory.

commitResults.messageTitle: Load saved tasks from ./data/bot.txt on startup (read path)
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds Storage.load(), which parses the pipe-separated data file back
into Todo/Deadline/Event objects. Bot now populates the initial task
list from Storage.load() instead of always starting empty. Missing
file/folder is treated as an empty list (happy path for now); the file
not existing on a fresh machine's first run is the expected case.

Verified manually that a task added and marked done in one run of
Bot is present with the same state when a second run lists tasks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle corrupted data file and load-time errors (stretch goal)
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage.load() now parses each line independently: a line that doesn't
match the expected "type | done | description[...]" shape (unknown
type letter, non-0/1 done flag, missing field) is skipped rather than
crashing or discarding the whole file, and a description of what was
wrong with it (with its line number) is collected into a warnings
list. Bot prints those warnings once at startup, inside the usual
divider block, so the user can see that some saved tasks couldn't be
read, then carries on with whatever tasks did parse successfully.

An IOException while reading the file at all (as opposed to a
malformed line within it) still surfaces as a BotException, consistent
with how save() already reports disk errors.

Manually verified: a data file mixing well-formed lines with an
unknown type, a bad done flag, and a line missing fields entirely
loads the good lines and reports the bad ones without losing data or
crashing. Missing ./data folder and missing data file at first run are
both already handled (Files.exists check), per the Level 7 notes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover save/load persistence in the UI test plan
commitResults.messageBody:
Bot now persists tasks to ./data/bot.txt across runs (Level 7), which
breaks the old assumption that every test case starts from a clean
in-memory slate: state can now leak between test cases via that file
unless it's handled explicitly. Update test/ui-test-plan.md's "How to
run" section and the test-ui skill to say a test case's Setup note
(default: delete ./data first) governs how the data file is prepared,
and to support test cases with multiple numbered Session blocks that
deliberately share one ./data across several separate program runs.

Add two new test cases exercising Level 7 directly:
- Test Case 7 runs two sessions sharing ./data and checks that tasks
  added/marked done in Session 1 reload with the same state in
  Session 2.
- Test Case 8 pre-seeds a data file mixing well-formed lines with an
  unknown type letter, a bad done flag, and a line missing fields, and
  checks the program reports each bad line and keeps the good ones
  instead of crashing or discarding everything (the stretch goal).

Ran the full updated plan (all 8 test cases, 9 program runs including
Test Case 7's two sessions) against the built program; every run's
output matches its expected block exactly.

Merges Level 7 (Save): the task list is now written to
./data/bot.txt after every change and reloaded from there on
startup, using a relative, OS-independent path built with
java.nio.file.Paths. Handles a missing ./data folder or data file on
first run (starts with an empty list) and a corrupted data file
(skips and reports malformed lines individually instead of crashing
or discarding everything). Also extends the UI test plan with
persistence and corrupted-file test cases and updates the test-ui
skill to handle them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parse deadline/event dates as real dates instead of free text
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds TaskDateTime, a small wrapper around java.time.LocalDate/
LocalDateTime that accepts "yyyy-MM-dd" (date only) or "yyyy-MM-dd
HHmm" (date and 24-hour time) on input - both for user commands and
for reading the data file back - and displays them as e.g. "Oct 15
2019" or "Oct 15 2019, 2:00PM" depending on whether a time was
given. Deadline's "by" and Event's "from"/"to" now hold a
TaskDateTime instead of a String, so "deadline return book /by
2019-10-15" is understood as an actual date rather than an opaque
label, per Level 8's minimal requirement.

Storage's save/load format is updated to match (dates are written and
read in the same yyyy-MM-dd[ HHmm] shape TaskDateTime parses), and the
deadline/event usage messages now show a valid example date instead
of "Sunday"/"Mon 2pm". This changes the accepted input format for
deadline/event dates and the on-disk data format from Level 7 - not
backward compatible with old free-text dates, which is expected for a
still-early-stage course project.

Also adds the Level 8 stretch goal: a new "on <yyyy-MM-dd>" command
that lists tasks occurring on a given date (Task#occursOn, overridden
by Deadline to match its "by" date and by Event to match any date in
its "from".."to" range; Todo never matches, since it has no date).

Manually verified: adding dated deadlines/events displays them in the
new format, "on" correctly finds a deadline exactly on a date and an
event spanning across it, an invalid date string is rejected with a
clear message instead of crashing, and the data file round-trips
through save and a fresh load unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover Level 8 dates/times in the UI test plan
commitResults.messageBody:
deadline/event no longer accept arbitrary free-text dates - they now
require yyyy-MM-dd or yyyy-MM-dd HHmm - so every existing test case
using a free-text date ("Sunday", "June 6th", "Aug 6th 2pm", ...)
would fail against the current program. Update Test Cases 3, 6, and 7
to use real dates and their formatted ("Jun 06 2019", "Aug 06 2019,
2:00PM") display output, and extend Test Case 5 with an invalid-date
line for deadline, event, and the new on command, plus the updated
"don't understand" message listing on among the commands.

Add Test Case 9, dedicated to the on <yyyy-MM-dd> stretch-goal command:
checks a deadline matches only its exact date, an event matches any
date within its from..to range (including a date that's neither
endpoint), a date with nothing scheduled prints an empty list, and a
Todo (no date) never matches.

Ran the full updated plan (9 test cases, 10 program runs including
Test Case 7's two sessions) against the built program; every run's
output matches its expected block exactly.

- Split Bot#main() into smaller private methods (printWelcome,
  loadTasks, runCommandLoop, executeCommand, printFarewell) instead of
  one method doing startup, loading, the whole command loop, and
  teardown. Kept it plain method extraction within Bot.java rather
  than introducing separate Ui/Parser/Command classes, since that's a
  bigger restructuring than this fix warrants on its own.
- Declare the task list as List<Task> (with new ArrayList<>() as the
  implementation) instead of ArrayList<Task>, both in main and in
  saveTasks's parameter, reducing coupling to a specific List
  implementation.
- Extract the shared "lead-in line, task, new count" structure out of
  printAdded/printRemoved into a private printTaskCountUpdate helper;
  the two methods now just supply their own lead-in text.
- Rename the 1-based local variable in parseTaskIndex from index to
  taskNumber, since it only becomes a 0-based index on the final
  "return taskNumber - 1" line - the old name was misleading for
  every line before that.
- Narrow Task's description/isDone fields to private (description
  also final, since it's never reassigned after construction), adding
  protected getDescription()/isDone() accessors. Needed updating
  Todo/Deadline/Event's toSaveFormat(), which read these fields
  directly - contrary to the review comment's assumption that
  subclasses only used inherited methods, added in the Level 7 commit
  that introduced toSaveFormat(), after this review had been done.

Rebuilt and reran the full UI test plan (9 test cases, 10 program
runs) against the refactored code; every run's output is byte-for-byte
unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-Level-8: understand deadline/event dates and times
commitResults.messageBody:
Merges Level 8 (Dates and Times): deadline's "/by" and event's
"/from"/"/to" are now parsed as real dates via a new TaskDateTime
wrapper around java.time.LocalDate/LocalDateTime, accepting
"yyyy-MM-dd" or "yyyy-MM-dd HHmm" and displaying as e.g.
"Oct 15 2019" or "Oct 15 2019, 6:00PM" - instead of storing
whatever text was typed. Adds the stretch goal: an "on <yyyy-MM-dd>"
command that lists tasks occurring on a given date (Task#occursOn,
matched exactly for a Deadline and by range for an Event; a Todo has
no date and never matches).

Also folds in a round of PR review fixes from @gabriel-wan on the
pre-Level-7 code: main() split into smaller private methods, the task
list typed as List<Task> instead of ArrayList<Task>, printAdded/
printRemoved's shared structure extracted into one helper,
parseTaskIndex's 1-based local renamed from index to taskNumber, and
Task's description/isDone fields narrowed to private (description also
final) with protected accessors added for the subclasses that read
them in toSaveFormat().

Updates the UI test plan's date-bearing test cases to the new
yyyy-MM-dd(HHmm) format and adds test cases for invalid-date errors
and the on command; all 9 test cases (10 program runs) pass.
